title: Early ideas of rule by people
description:
Ancient city-states (notably Athens) experiment with citizen participation.
	Note: citizenship was limited; many groups were excluded.

title: Magna Carta and limits on rulers
description: Early step toward rule of law: the ruler's powers are not unlimited and are constrained by law/agreements.

title: Glorious Revolution (England)
description: Parliamentary supremacy strengthens; the idea that rulers must be accountable to representative institutions gains ground.

title: American Revolution
description: Representative government and constitutional ideas spread through modern revolutions.

title: French Revolution
description: Ideas of liberty, equality and popular sovereignty influence democratic movements worldwide.

title: Expansion of voting rights
description:
In many countries, struggles for universal adult franchise grow.
	Voting rights expand gradually beyond property-owning men.

title: Post–World War II democratic wave
description: New constitutions, decolonization and mass movements push many countries toward elections and representative government.

title: Third wave of democracy
description: Several authoritarian regimes fall; multi-party elections and civil liberties become key global demands.

title: Democracy as a working ideal
description:
Democracy understood through core features: elected rulers, final decision-making by elected representatives, free and fair elections, political equality, and constitutional limits/rights.
	Debates continue about quality of democracy, inclusion, and accountability.
